Since the failed run, the branch has moved from `c700b3204283` to `6f72a89a5052`, the commit the triage's check-run context named. Work against that current head. No GitHub fact shows `main` failing, so a separate `main` fix (B or C) is not justified.
Q2: In this checkout, `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` uses the fresh `query_pull_requests(slug, branch, cwd)` lookup in `_evaluate_mcp_push` at line 2279. That is the security hardening the PR made, so reverting it (B) would undo the PR's purpose. C cannot work: CI never prepares security hooks under `.claude/hooks/**` and requires their live copies to match the templates. So the live copy must take the template's content. That path is an automation path, so it must be listed exactly in `files_touched`.
Q3: If the current head already passes the parity test and CI, nothing is broken. The parity test `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` already guards against this drift, so a new regression test (B) would only duplicate it.

SETUP REQUIRED:
- None. The live-copy edit only needs the existing `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true` (the default) and an exact `files_touched` entry for `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`. If the automation-path guard rejects that entry because of who wrote the issue, the issue will move to `ai:scope-blocked` and the unblock judge will pick it up. Nobody has to provision anything first.

Assumptions:
- The planner treats `ai/issue-6824` as both the base and the target of the fix.
- Before editing, the implementer runs `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` on the current branch head (`6f72a89a5052`) to confirm the failure is still there.
